This ciphersuite uses edwards448 for the Group and SHAKE256 for the hash function H meant to produce Ed448-compliant signatures as specified in Section 5.2
 of [RFC8032]. Unlike Ed448 in [RFC8032], this ciphersuite does not allow applications to specify a context string and always sets the context of [RFC8032] to the

This ciphersuite uses edwards448 for the Group and SHAKE256 for the hash function H meant to produce Ed448-compliant signatures as specified in Section 5.2
 of [RFC8032]. Unlike Ed448 in [RFC8032], this ciphersuite does not allow applications to specify a context string and always sets the context of [RFC8032] to the
 empty string. The value of the (internal to FROST) contextString parameter is "FROST-ED448-SHAKE256-v1".

orig_text: Note that the lambda_i value derived during this procedure does not change across FROST signing operations for the same signing group. As such, participants can compute it once and store it for reuse across signing sessions.
correct_text: Note that the lambda_i value derived during this procedure depends only on the participant list and the participant's identifier. As such, participants can compute lambda_i once for each participant list and store it for reuse across signing sessions that use the same participant list.
notes:
This is mostly a clarification, as:
"Signing group" is not a defined term in the document, and lambda_i is a function of the participant list of the current signing operation, which varies between sessions when min_participants < max_participants. Caching lambda_i across sessions with different participant lists yields invalid signatures
